body.p: Index length Index space This chapter discusses two of the most important questions when dealing with indexes: knowing how long the index should be and reducing the size of an index (either by employing typographic means or actually reducing the length of the index) to fit the space available.

section.title: Average/Appropriate Index Lengths
section.p: Index lengthby material type Trade books Reference books Index length varies dramatically based on the type of material being indexed. Mass market and trade books typically have indexes that run 2–5% of the text length. General reference books average 7–8%. Technical documentation may require 10% or more, and specialized material such as legal texts can require indexes of 15% or even higher.

section.title: Reducing the Index Space
section.p: Space reduction techniques When the index exceeds the allotted space, several options exist. Typographic changes such as reducing the font size, adjusting leading, or switching from indented to run-in style can save space without cutting content.

Columns, numbers of Typography in indexes The number of columns affects the total space required for the index. Switching from two to three columns, while reducing the width of each entry, can sometimes save a page or more.
